Hard mode is on. You must interact with this reminder before using the device.
"Why are you opening your phone right "
Dint helps you pause before you unlock your phone. It asks what you are about to do, so you can use your phone with intention instead of opening it out of boredom, impulse, or habit.

Most screen-time tools step in after you are already using your phone. Dint steps in earlier, right at unlock, when the habit usually starts. The goal is not guilt or punishment. It is to make the moment conscious enough that you can choose what happens next and self reflect on your intention.
Dint is not meant to block urgent access. If you need your phone right away for safety, health, travel, or another real-world need, use the emergency skip ("NOW") and keep moving.
Dint steps in when you unlock your phone and asks why you are unlocking it. The goal is simple: help you use your phone on purpose.
When you unlock your phone, Dint shows a prompt before you can continue.
You choose or type why you are opening your phone, whether it is useful or just a habit.
Make unlocking your phone intentional again
Based on your reason it locks your phone or you keep using it as usual.

Why do banking apps warn about this?

Android tells apps whenever any accessibility service is turned on for the device, not just what that service actually does. Some banking and wallet apps show a warning any time an accessibility service is enabled, including Dint\'s. This is normal Android behavior and outside Dint\'s control.

Android does not let normal apps replace the lock screen. Dint uses an accessibility service to step in right after unlock, ask for a reason, log answers on-device, and support reminders, hard mode, and lock actions.
Allows the app to lock the device again when you decide you did not actually want to unlock it.
Needed only for the explicit hard lock action. Without it, the app can still close the session and send you home, but it cannot force a full device relock.
